newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Comfy raises $23.9 mln in Tel Aviv IPO.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Comfy raises $23.9 mln in Tel Aviv IPO.

text.p: An inital public offering in Israel's Comfy Interactive Movies Ltd was 30 percent oversubscribed and raised 100 million shekels ($29.3 million), an underwriter said on Thursday.
"The total amount for the offer was 130 million shekels," the spokesman for Leader Securities Underwriting said.
Half the offering of 12.5 million new shares, which sold for eight shekels each, had been taken up earlier in an institutional tranche mainly to European investors.
"Because of the 30 percent oversubscription, new subscribers will receive an allotment of 60 percent," the spokesman said.

Prior to the offering Comfy's share capital comprised 31.18 million shares outstanding held by Shamrock Holdings, the investment arm of the Roy Disney family, as well as Bank Hapoalim, Israeli investment bank Dovrat Shrem and the U.S. investment house Cowen & Co.

Comfy designs and manufacturers computer keyboards and software designed for young children. The offering was a rare instance of a high-tech start-up opting to float domestically rather than on Nasdaq.
